category.name: INTERNAL
category.code: A framework invariant was violated; this is a defect, not a user input problem.

category.name: CAPABILITY
category.code: The request needs a capability this build does not provide, or that the architecture rules out.

category.name: RESOURCE
category.code: A configured memory, size or count budget would be exceeded; no work was dropped silently.

category.name: USAGE
category.code: The first argument is not a known command.
The option is not defined for this command.
A required option was not given.
An option that takes a value was last or followed by another option.
An option value does not have the required form.
A non-repeatable option was given more than once.
A positional argument was given where none is accepted.

category.name: CONFIG
category.code: The configuration file cannot be opened or decoded as UTF-8.
A configuration line is not valid properties syntax.
A key is defined twice in one source; there is no silent last-wins.
A cf.* key is not defined by this build.
A value cannot be parsed or is outside its allowed range.
Individually valid values contradict each other.
A legacy key was recognised and mapped to a target key.
A legacy key belongs to a mechanism the architecture removed; it is deliberately not acted on.
A legacy key requests behaviour the architecture rules out (database, process, sandbox).
A legacy key has no disposition for where it was found (not in the legacy settings catalog, or not a properties key there); it is refused, never passed through or dropped.
A legacy key requests retained behaviour that a later work package implements; a run refuses it until then.
Under the legacy parsing rules a value means something other than it says (for example 'yes' read as false); the legacy meaning is imported.
cf.execution.sut names no SUT plugin found on the application class path or on cf.execution.classpath, and is not generated-java.
Two SUT plugins on the class path have the id cf.execution.sut names; neither is chosen silently.

category.name: KEY
category.code: A key label does not fit the selected encoding.
A key label equals the encoding's reserved sentinel value.
Rows of different key encodings were combined.
The plan's labels do not fit the requested encoding policy.
Value labels moved into a signed window because positive-only numbering did not fit the selected encoding.
The parse consumed a different number of keys than the census counted.
Text is not a well-formed key list such as [1, -2, 3].
A key frame header carries impossible values.
A key frame ends before its header or declared payload does.
A key frame payload ends in the middle of a key.
A key frame's declared key count disagrees with its payload byte count.
A key frame has a schema version this build does not read.
A key frame names an encoding this build does not know.
Bytes follow the end of a key frame that should have been consumed exactly.
A legacy input only worked because a counter wrapped around; there is no equivalence promise for it.

category.name: INPUT
category.code: The input file or stream cannot be opened or read.
The input's format cannot be told from its file name; there is no silent fallback to another format.
The input is not well formed in its own format.
The input is well formed but does not have the shape of a schedule.
The input uses YAML or TOML syntax outside the supported schedule subset.
Two sheets share a name, ignoring case.
The input exceeds a format limit or a configured size bound.
The document declares a protocol or format version this build does not read; nothing of it is used (fail closed).
An fwgen spec has something the legacy compiler's compatibility mode warned about and went on with: an unknown field is ignored, or a slot will not produce what its author probably meant.

category.name: SPEC
category.code: A data cell starts with FW_ but is not a cell directive this framework knows.
A cell directive has a missing or malformed argument.
FW_Optional or FW_RefineCodeExceptQuoted has no earlier value in its own sheet to apply to.
A row of a control sheet is incomplete or holds a value of the wrong kind.
A sheet named FW_... is not a control sheet this framework knows; it is ignored, as the legacy parser did.
A formula cell is kept as its formula text and is not evaluated.
The FW_RunMeFirstOnce cell is not a class RunMeFirstOnce with a public static String FW_ARGS.
A sheet repeats a value; duplicates stay distinct keys, as the legacy parser kept them.

category.name: PLAN
category.code: The scenario has no FW_Seq sheet, or it holds no row with content; there is nothing to generate.
A FW_Seq row or directive refers to a sheet that does not exist and was not generated.
A FW_Seq cell starts with FW_ but is not a flag or directive this framework knows.
A FW_Seq directive does not match its grammar.
Joiners wait for each other's tables in a circle, so no order of evaluation exists.
A later FW_Seq row for the same sheet replaces the directives of an earlier one; the flags of the earlier row stay (the documented overwrite rule, which real scenarios use routinely).
A FW_Seq row names no sheet of its own and takes over the target of an earlier row, as the legacy parser did.
A FW_Seq cell is neither a sheet name nor an FW_ token and is ignored.
A reference named no sheet, so an empty virtual sheet was generated for it, as the legacy parser did.
A sheet carries flags that cannot both apply; only the first one counts, as in the legacy parser.

category.name: GENERATION
category.code: A sheet produced no rows. A mandatory sheet without rows leaves no candidates under the default empty-stage policy; the legacy Core dropped such a sheet instead.
A later pass found no rows to work on because no earlier directive of the sheet generated any.
A grouped row rewritten by FW_ReplaceRE is no longer a list of key labels and is dropped (legacy policy warn); the diagnostic counts the dropped rows and names the first one.
A FW_ReplaceRE replacement cannot be applied to a row's key text (for example a reference to a missing group).
A joined FW_ReplaceRE names a sheet without values; the legacy Core left that replacement out.
A joiner reads a table that an earlier joiner consumed (no FW_Reuse), so it reads no rows.
A FW_ReplaceRE pattern needs text that a key-label list never contains, so it can never match (cf.generation.replace.pattern warn; strict refuses the plan).
A FW_ReplaceRE pattern changed no row of its sheet (cf.generation.replace.unmatched warn; fail stops the run).
A FW_ReplaceRE pattern equals its replacement: it changes nothing but the plan's identity (cf.generation.replace.identity warn).
Per grouped sheet: rows seen, rewritten and dropped, and the rows each FW_ReplaceRE pattern changed (cf.generation.replace.diagnostics summary).

category.name: CONSTRAINT
category.code: A constraint sidecar or legacy bonds file is missing, unreadable, not UTF-8 or not in its format; nothing of it is applied.
A constraint sidecar entry has an invalid shape, type or key; an authored rule is never dropped silently.
A constraint, parameter or order names a sheet the scenario does not have.
A constraint names a sheet that is no column of the candidates (excluded, heading, consumed, empty and dropped, or without directives), so it could never fire.
A 'when' predicate is outside the supported expression grammar or uses a name it may not use.
A scenario has a companion constraint sidecar and a different constraint file is configured.
A scenario's companion constraint sidecar (<stem>.constraints.json beside it) was read, as the legacy loader read it.
A rule or part of one can never match: a value no cell of its sheet has, or a pairs entry without every sheet.

category.name: ASSEMBLY
category.code: A mandatory sheet has no rows, so no candidate exists under the default empty-stage policy; zero candidates are executable and nothing passed.
cf.generation.emptyStagePolicy=LEGACY_DROP_WITH_DIAGNOSTIC dropped a mandatory sheet without rows from the candidates, as the legacy Core did; the candidates no longer contain that column.
A mandatory sheet has no first row, so a baseline reference to it cannot be resolved; no value is invented.
cf.assembly.mandatoryLimit kept only the first rows of the mandatory product or of an optional subset's product.
An optional subset whose product of rows exceeds cf.optional.subsetRowLimit was left out, as the legacy Core did.
An optional combination size is larger than the number of optional sheets, so it forms no combination.
A rule could not be evaluated on a candidate (a type error, a value outside a declared order); the run stops.
Covering selection cannot run on this plan (product above cf.coverage.hardCap, no mandatory sheet to cover).
Some t-tuples of the mandatory sheets' rows appear in no row the rules allow; they are reported as infeasible, not as uncovered.
A candidate's source could not be rendered (a value too complex to refine, a label without a value).

category.name: EXECUTION
category.code: The candidate's generated Java source does not compile; the sample is BROKEN and the compiler's messages are kept with it.
This Java runtime has no system Java compiler (javax.tools), so generated sources cannot be compiled; the samples are INFRA_FAIL. Run on a JDK, not a bare JRE image.
The generated class has no public static void main(String[]) to run; the sample is BROKEN.
The sample produced no verdict: the plugin returned none, or the generated class has no static int field FW_VAR or FW_CUSTOM_VAR (the one cf.execution.verdict selects); the sample is BROKEN.
The system under test threw; the sample is BROKEN, never a domain failure, unless the plugin itself turned the exception into a domain observation.
The generated class calls System.exit, Runtime.exit or Runtime.halt, which would stop the whole virtual machine; it is not run and the sample is BROKEN.
The plugin's oracle judged the observation unusable (BROKEN or an outcome an oracle may not give).
The cooperative deadline cf.execution.timeout.millis passed; the sample was asked to stop and is TIMEOUT.

The sample did not stop within cf.execution.cancel.grace.millis after its deadline. Its thread was interrupted and left running: one JVM cannot stop it. The sample is TIMEOUT; the run reports the thread.
The SUT plugin could not open a session for the sample; the sample is INFRA_FAIL.
A SUT session threw while closing; the sample keeps its outcome and the run reports the failure.
The virtual machine ran out of memory while the sample ran; the sample is INFRA_FAIL.
The sample was deliberately not attempted (a stop policy or an earlier failure ended the run first); it is SKIPPED.
The run was cancelled before or while the sample ran; the sample is CANCELLED.
FW_RunMeFirstOnce did not compile, run or leave a String FW_ARGS, so no candidate can run; the legacy executor stopped too.
Some samples ignored their deadline and their threads were still running when the run ended; they were not stopped, because one JVM cannot stop them.

cf.execution.coverage=lines could not measure some samples (the candidate has no executable line of its own, or its instrumented bytecode could not be built); their coverage metrics are omitted, never invented.

category.name: RESULT
category.code: A second observation for an existing sample key differs from the committed one; the committed one stays and the conflict is an error, never an overwrite.
A listener kept failing on a committed observation: it was offered the same observation again, with its sample key, then skipped. Counters come from the committed results, never from deliveries.
Attachments did not fit cf.results.maxAttachmentBytes and were not kept; the observations they belong to are unchanged and the omissions are counted.
Writing an optional report or export failed; the committed observations and their verdicts are unchanged.
Writing a checkpoint failed; the last good checkpoint was kept and the committed observations are unchanged.

category.name: ANALYSIS
category.code: An analysis goal is malformed: its key, its mode (min, max or target), its target or its weight (finite, at least 0).
An objective expression does not parse or names an unknown variable or function; nothing is evaluated.
An objective or metric value is NaN or infinite; it is refused, never coerced into a number.
Formal analysis needs declared goals and at least one eligible sample; it does not discover axes.
Triage was asked to fail on findings and the run has at least one distinct finding; the report was still written.

category.name: CAMPAIGN
category.code: A seed cannot drive a bias: none of its winners carries sheet selections (a legacy seed was joined to database rows, which this build does not keep), so nothing was run.
An iteration produced no seed with front winners (no analysis, or no eligible sample with metrics), so the next iteration cannot be derived; the iterations before it stand.
The seed carried no narrowing signal (CONVERGED_NO_SIGNAL): the iteration ran without bias and the campaign stopped after it, as the legacy iterate loop did.
The next iteration would have no candidate to run (the bias would keep fewer than one, or no candidate was executable); the campaign stopped and the iterations before it stand.

category.name: CHECKPOINT
category.code: A checkpoint is unreadable, truncated, of an unknown schema or fails its payload checksum; nothing was resumed.
A checkpoint does not belong to what would be resumed: scenario, plan, dictionary, policy, plugin or configuration differ; nothing was resumed.

category.name: RUN
category.code: The work was cancelled cooperatively before it finished; nothing it had not completed was published.
The run's time budget (cf.run.budget.millis) passed: admission stopped and running samples were cancelled cooperatively; what was committed before stays.
A run's totals do not reconcile: a stage invariant failed, which is a defect of the framework, never a property of the scenario; the committed observations are kept.
The run's stop policy ended admission (cf.run.stop.candidates or cf.run.stop.target); the candidates admitted before the decision finished, and the decision does not depend on workers or timing.
The run's error budget (cf.run.stop.errors) was used up by BROKEN, TIMEOUT or INFRA_FAIL verdict samples: admission ended and the command fails; what was committed stays.
The doctor found a blocking check: a run would fail on this environment as configured; the report names it.
